[[credential-scoping]] and [[runtime-paths]] are not independent decisions — they
implement the same architectural principle applied to two different concerns.

**Credential Scoping** centralizes all Anthropic API key provisioning at a single point:
a secrets loader reads from a git-ignored `.env` file and injects the key directly into
the child process environment immediately at spawn time. The Hub's own process environment
never holds the credential; downstream code (the Ingest or Query agent) simply consumes
what it was handed, immutably. This eliminates any risk that a compromised Hub process
could leak credentials by inspecting its own ambient environment.

**Runtime Path Configuration** applies the identical pattern to file locations: a single
path resolver consumes configuration (command line, environment, config file, or code
defaults) at startup, validates that every required input exists, and publishes the
resolved set to all downstream code. No other part of the codebase reads the ambient
working directory directly; everything downstream is handed an already-resolved path set.

Both decisions reject the alternative of scattering responsibility — leaving credentials
loose in inherited environment variables, or allowing every component to discover its own
paths by reading the working directory. Instead, both centralize the decision once, at a
known moment (startup), and enforce that everything else consumes the result passively.

This coupling matters when reasoning about which architectural changes can be made independently:
adding a new runtime location requires extending the single resolver (one place to touch);
adding a new credential-dependent service requires extending the single secrets-injection
mechanism (one place to touch). Conversely, if either centralizing mechanism were bypassed
or duplicated downstream, both security (for credentials) and configuration stability (for
paths) would degrade together.

## Answer

Your credential-scoping and runtime-path decisions are deeply coupled—they implement the same architectural principle applied to two different concerns.

According to [[credential-scoping]], the Anthropic API key is never held in the Hub's own process environment. Instead, a secrets loader reads it from a `.env` file and injects it directly into the child process environment at spawn time. The Hub itself never touches the credential; downstream code simply consumes what it was handed, immutably.

[[runtime-paths]] applies exactly the same pattern to file locations: a single path resolver consumes configuration at startup, validates every required input, and publishes the resolved set to all downstream code. No other component reads the ambient working directory directly; everything consumes the already-resolved paths.

Both decisions reject scattering responsibility. Instead, both centralize the decision once (at startup) and enforce that everything else consumes the result passively. This means:

- **Security and stability degrade together**: if either the secrets-injection or path-resolver mechanisms were bypassed or duplicated downstream, both credential security and configuration stability would suffer.
- **New changes stay localized**: adding a new runtime location or new credential-dependent service means extending one resolver each, not touching multiple parts of the codebase.

I've saved this connection as a new page, [[concepts/credential-and-path-scoping-coupling]], which details how these two decisions reinforce a single architectural principle: a single authoritative point for each concern, with no ambient mutable process state.
